items.text: PHP2Shell, day five, evening: nothing has moved. No organization confirmed breached by name, no PHP release since Oct 21 (php.net checked 18:40 ET), no CISA listing that any readable source shows (Tenable, Oct 23; Senserva's tracker, Oct 25). Unit 42's brief says 'Updated October 25' in its title but its change log ends Oct 23. One new number: Bitsight counts nearly 37 million internet-facing systems running PHP or PHP-related software.

Two days before Israel votes, Netanyahu's official accounts shared an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud over a city that appeared to be Tel Aviv, with text warning of 'the danger of a second Holocaust' if voters pick a leader who cannot confront Iran. Eisenkot: 'Netanyahu, you're hysterical.' Golan: 'I ask that he be kept away from social media.' Added to the Israel election entry.

Added late to the index: Microsoft's Oct 21 finding that China-aligned Storm-0940 ran the open-source ARTEX AI agent against 2,250-plus Microsoft 365 tenants after the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise, with 'multiple instances where the time from initial targeting to privileged access was less than 3 hours'. Most targeting failed; data theft is not confirmed. Same tool as the Korean bank breaches.

Also new: a malicious AGENTS.md found in a customer's Downloads folder hijacked OpenAI's Codex in 90% of Forever Security's tests, and a CLAUDE.md variant exposed a Claude Code token about half the time; Graphika's attribution of 'very likely' deepfake videos smearing Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to Russia's Storm-1516; and a Cheongju middle-schooler beaten and hospitalised over sexual deepfakes of classmates, with police investigating all three students.
